REVISED rationale (was: 'no source at all'; now: 'sources found, but conflicting'). The recovered eagle-lng.com archive (2019 capture, describing a later-stage FSRU design) states the terminal itself is '4-8 bcma' (max 8 bcma), separate from a '10 bcma' pipeline capacity. The recovered energiafalcione.com archive (2009 capture, describing an earlier onshore design) states '8 billion cubic meters/year...that can be increased to 12 bcm/yr'. Neither figure, under the project's own 1 mtpa = 1.36 bcm/y conversion factor, cleanly reconciles to the stored 8.10 mtpa (which implies ~11.0 bcm/y) -- and the two company sources themselves disagree with each other (8-12 bcm/y onshore vs 4-8 bcma floating), reflecting a project that evidently changed design between 2008/9 and its later FSRU concept. This is genuinely conflicting data across the sponsor's own two self-published sites, not an absence of sourcing -- staging as a deletion (rather than guessing which figure/design-era to convert) pending reviewer judgment; see companion qa record for the full detail.
